analysis:
Examined the supplied batch: release-swift.yml (head full text, with the diff adding path filters), two changelog.d entries and docs/architecture/inference.md (patch plus partial base text). No executable provider code is in this batch.

release-swift.yml: the only changes are four new master-push path filters (provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, verify-nemotron-prompt-parity.sh, provider-test-shards.py). The filters only widen what triggers the staging lane, which is still gated by vars.STAGING_ENABLED == 'true'. Prod stays tag-gated or dispatch-gated, and the workflow comments state that resolve-provider-release.sh refuses prod on non-tag triggers. The new paths do not touch the signing-identity routing or add secret exposure; `secrets: inherit` is unchanged. Path filters cannot cause a prod release.

Changelog and docs: these describe new behavior that is implemented outside this batch. A release can register `cluster_runtime` facts, including a per-model pair-serving grant and parity qualifications, with the coordinator, gated per environment by *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED variables. Those facts feed automatic coordinator approval of two-Mac clusters and public cluster traffic for GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B. The changelog admits these rest on an owner decision and DevNet results, not on a pipeline run on M5 Ultras. This is relevant to TB-011, T-054, T-055 and T-056 (qualification evidence, overclaiming trust), and to TB-002. The coordinator-side acceptance is platform-owned and outside this repo. A part-health.json split fixes a supervisor liveness restart (availability only); I saw no security regression.

Unverified contracts for later passes: the actual Swift implementations (ClusterPublicModels, DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant, ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release), the release scripts and the reusable release-provider.yml. They need review to confirm that digests are computed from the final signed app, that the grant is not attacker-influenced, and that the registration is authenticated. The threat model has no dedicated entry for the cluster pair-serving grant and auto-approval, which is a possible threat-model documentation gap, not a finding on this evidence.
